# Independent idle isolation architecture review

Reviewed 2026-11-04 against ECU base commit `497aabb4a0ea686b240182e42b4c64aefa280c32`. This is a read-only architecture review, not a final netlist, routing, manufacturing or powered acceptance. Root proposes and implements the new revision. No production file was changed by this reviewer; no subagents, services, hardware writes, eFuse writes, vendor messages or purchases were used.

The initial direct-LED/HCT14 proposal had concrete electrical specification gaps. The revised buffered optical inputs, ordinary TTL NOR, separately regulated actuator rail and supervisor-gated driver are a reasonable architecture to develop. They can remove the intended DC coil-return path through J1 while retaining independent RUN gating. **No physical release is approved.** The final routed revision, exact parts and fault behavior still need review and measurement.

## Findings that changed the proposal

1. **High: RUN_5V cannot directly source the proposed LED current with its guaranteed logic-high specification.** Archived A4 U9 is SN74HCT08N, with a 4 mA VOH test and an existing 10 kΩ R47 load. A 6N137 needs up to 5 mA to recognize an on input, before R47. The revised proposal buffers both LEDs using input-side TO92 2N3904s and carrier 5 V. Keeping J1 pin3 as carrier 5 V is compatible with isolation when it feeds only input-side components. [TI HCT08](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hct08.pdf), electrical table; [Vishay 6N137](https://www.vishay.com/docs/84732/6n137_vo2601_vo2611.pdf), pp.3-4.

2. **Medium: the original Schmitt inverter has no guaranteed low-transition margin.** 6N137 VOL can be 0.6 V, while SN74HCT14's falling threshold can be 0.5 V at 4.5 V. A permitted opto low need not cross that threshold. Revised SN74HCT02N uses ordinary TTL inputs with VIL 0.8 V, giving 0.2 V specified low margin. NOR of the two active-low opto outputs asserts drive only when both LEDs are on. Tie unused gate inputs to a defined local rail; leave their outputs NC. [HCT14](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hct14.pdf), §6.5; [HCT02](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74hct02.pdf), §§4-5.

3. **High: gate-driver UVLO alone does not cover undefined isolator/logic operation.** UCC27524 can leave UVLO below the 4.5 V minimum operating supply of the opto and HCT logic. The revised proposal uses local MCP100 RESET_n to hold ENA low, with a mandatory external pulldown. This adds a real validity gate instead of trusting the NOR during an invalid rail. MCP100-485 trips in 4.60-4.85 V, giving 0.10 V static margin above 4.5 V. Its reset assertion delay is only specified as 10 µs typical, with no maximum; its hysteresis is 50 mV typical, with no maximum. No arbitrary fast-brownout fail-low guarantee follows. Release is 150-700 ms. [MCP100](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/11187f.pdf), p.2; [UCC27524](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ucc27524.pdf), §6.5.

4. **Medium: the first regulator accuracy assumption was too narrow.** LM2931A's 4.81-5.19 V figures are at 25°C, VIN14 V and IO10 mA. Its full-range/100 mA bound is 4.75-5.25 V, and its output needs at least 100 µF with a qualifying ESR. This gives inadequate assured release headroom for the selected supervisor. Root changed to LM317AT/NOPB, described below. [LM2931A](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm2931-n.pdf), pp.3/5/10. Rendered pages were inspected because font weight identifies full-temperature limits.

5. **Medium: loaded GPIO and NPN saturation are not full-temperature guarantees.** Espressif's VOH entry is measured with high-impedance load; 40 mA source current is a typical 25°C figure. The onsemi 2N3904 saturation limits are likewise 25°C, at specific collector/base currents. The proposed low-mA buffer input is sensible, but a calculation assuming loaded GPIO ≥2.64 V and VCEsat≤0.3 V is conditional. Measure loaded GPIO, LED current and storage delay on the actual module across the declared operating range. [ESP32-S3](https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf), Table5-4; [2N3904](https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/2n3903-d.pdf), p.2.

6. **Medium: a 1% duty check does not cover the physical range accepted by the software.** `idle_command.hpp` rounds arbitrary duty to integer microseconds; `PwmExecutor` permits high_us=1. A 1% pulse at 250 Hz is 40 µs, much longer. Opto/NPN/storage/gate delays can materially change sub-1% delivered energy. Establish a measured minimum reliable pulse or retain the gap explicitly while physical output remains disabled. Circuit sensitivity experiments must not silently replace all short pulses with ideal instant edges.

## Revised power and driver constraints

For LM317A, OUT-to-ADJ 120 Ω and ADJ-to-ACT_GND 374 Ω, both 1%, give these independent corner results using the full-temperature VREF1.225-1.270 V and IADJ0-100 µA:

| Quantity | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Static output rail | 4.967314-5.345904 V |
| Minimum divider load | 10.107 mA |
| Minimum headroom with 9 V at regulator input | 3.654 V |
| Minimum rail minus MCP100-485 maximum trip | 0.117314 V |
| Maximum rail margin below 5.5 V logic ceiling | 0.154096 V |

The divider alone meets the 10 mA minimum-load condition. The 3 V headroom requirement is met if the actual regulator input remains at least 9 V. Do not reuse this result after an unaccounted series protection drop. These are DC component/tolerance bounds, not transient overshoot, release-time or thermal qualification. LM317A TO220 is pin1 ADJ, pin2 and tab OUT, pin3 IN. OUT-to-IN protection diode is anode OUT/cathode IN. It does not protect against reverse input polarity. Local input/output decoupling and output capacitance need the application guidance and actual circuit measurements; this regulator does not inherit LM2931's mandatory ESR window. [TI LM317A](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm317a.pdf), §§6/7.5/8.4.

Carrier-side LED resistor 357 Ω, 1%, gives 7.6268-14.8544 mA under the proposed 4.75-5.25 V carrier rail and VCEsat≤0.3 V/VF≤1.7 V assumptions. The upper limit conservatively uses zero diode/transistor drop. This covers the opto's 7.5 mA switching-table input, not just its DC recognition current. The 100 ns opto delay limit also assumes RL350 Ω and CL15 pF; a different pullup, trace or gate load requires its own timing bound/measurement. Use local pullups on both outputs, pin7 tied locally high, and 100 nF between pins8/5 at each package. Pins1/4 are NC; LED2 is anode,3 cathode; output6, enable7, VCC8, ground5. [Vishay 6N137](https://www.vishay.com/docs/84732/6n137_vo2601_vo2611.pdf), pp.1/3/4.

Proposed 1 kΩ PWM and 1.8 kΩ RUN base resistors plus 100 kΩ base-emitter bias keep nominal source loads small. Including R47 and even a base-emitter short, the RUN resistor-path upper bound is 3.623 mA with 5% resistors and 5.25 V. This checks a loading budget, not saturation/storage across all temperatures. Use the exact 2N3904 pin contract, emitter1/base2/collector3; do not substitute BC547's different lead order.

MCP100 **D bondout** TO92 is pin1 RESET_n, pin2 VDD, pin3 VSS; H bondout swaps the first two. At its specified conditions, VOL≤0.6 V and VOH≥VDD-0.7 V support direct driver ENA gating; a 4.7 kΩ pulldown loads the supervisor by about 1.2 mA maximum. The current UCC27524 datasheet electrical tables name D/DGN/DSD and omit P even though the product offers PDIP. Freeze guaranteed P/P.B data for the actual procured part before powered acceptance. Do not borrow an arbitrary package's thresholds or 12 V peak-current conditions as a physical 5.2 V timing guarantee.

IRLZ44NPBF is a reasonable fast TO220 candidate: Infineon's product record is active and its datasheet specifies RDS(on) at 4 V, avoiding a threshold-voltage-as-on-voltage mistake. Pin1 gate, pin2 and tab drain, pin3 source. At 2 A, its 35 mΩ 25°C bound corresponds to 0.14 W conduction loss before hot resistance and switching losses. This is not a heatsink acceptance. It lacks the VNP's internal current/thermal protection and feedback. External protected fused switched power, fuse coordination, short tests and actual valve R/L remain mandatory. [Infineon product](https://www.infineon.com/part/IRLZ44N), [datasheet](https://www.infineon.com/assets/row/public/documents/24/49/infineon-irlz44n-datasheet-en.pdf).

I did not establish that VNP35N07-E intrinsically cannot support 1% PWM. Its documented fast switching uses 10 V/10 Ω drive, unlike the draft's 5 V/220 Ω. The higher-resistance table also has differing units across legacy and E-version records, so no interpolated physical delay is accepted here. A fast ordinary MOSFET simplifies the drive model, but loses smart-device protection. [ST datasheet](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/vnp35n07-e.pdf), Table7. The onsemi FQP30N06L current production status was not verified from an accessible primary product record, so I do not recommend it over the explicitly active Infineon candidate.

## Isolation, disconnects and remaining acceptance

The new design must keep all J1 conductors, both input transistors/LEDs and permanent GPIO3 strap bias on the carrier side. All detector logic, driver, regulator, flyback and power switch stay on ACT_GND. No shared copper zone, conductive mounting, debug cable, shield or unintended connector pin may bridge the domains. This low-voltage return isolation is not a certified mains/vehicle isolation rating.

The independent connectivity graph reproduces the old Q-source-to-J1 return and removes it under the proposed separation. A deliberate ACT_GND-to-CARRIER_GND bridge restores that path as a negative control. This is a DC topology result with intact optical barriers, not a device/SPICE transient simulation. An open carrier return can still cause bounded input-side/clamp currents; it does not create a 2 A coil path across an intact optical barrier. Measure the actual input currents and reverse junction stress, rather than stating every J1 pin carries zero current.

Signal-open or carrier5V loss should darken a relevant LED, making the local NOR low. Supervisor loss/invalid rail must hold ENA off. Base-emitter bias must be local at each NPN so an open signal does not float it. Zero/full duty and continuous RUN need DC testing as well as pulse testing. Coil current and mechanical closure decay after switch-off; a low driver command is not instantaneous closure or measured valve position.

An uninsulated MOS drain tab touching grounded case material bypasses PWM and RUN and can continuously energize the valve. The LM317 tab is the regulated rail, not ground. A FET drain-source short likewise defeats logic gating; an ordinary current fuse will not clear a normal-current stuck-on valve. Define an independent actuator-branch disconnect and its control before accepting that fault. All case hardware and heatsinks need explicit insulation/clearance contracts.

Permanent carrier-side GPIO3 pulldown/take-off, actual eFuse/JTAG routing and physical module geometry remain unresolved. Do not burn eFuses or enable the selected output to make a simulation pass. The final new carrier/accessory netlists and copper must independently reproduce the pin contract and isolation graph. Then use a current-limited resistor load and scope the rails, supervisor, RUN, GPIO, LED currents, gate/drain and load through startup/brownout/EN/reset/download, input and power return opens, failed output, watchdog/interlock and stalled producer. Validate an identified NC valve only after that fixture passes. Hardware output remains inhibited until those separate gates are met.

## Evidence and reproduction

`architecture_probe.py` / `architecture-probe.json` retain 16 regulator corners, the eight control truth-table rows, conditional LED/current envelopes and the DC path/negative-control graph. Run `python3 .cache/engine/idle-isolation-review/architecture_probe.py` from the repository. These checks intentionally do not model semiconductor switching, heat, EMI or mechanical fit.

`sources/manifest.json` records downloaded primary URLs, byte counts and SHA256, plus failed downloads. Some primary PDFs were read through the web tool when the direct host refused/timed out; no byte hash is claimed for those. Source PDFs, extracts and full-page renders are local research inputs, not for redistribution in the project evidence. `review-manifest.json` binds this report/probe and the unchanged source files inspected. A later final-design review must bind its own actual sources and results.
